turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey there, how have things been?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ah, it's been a long day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I left the tent stakes at home. We're already here and it's getting dark.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Don't panic, you can improvise. Are you on soft ground or a hard, rocky site?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good. Find straight, sturdy sticks about as thick as your thumb, sharpen one end with a knife or a rock, and push them in at an angle away from the tent.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Will that hold if it gets windy?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Mostly. You can also tie the guy lines to rocks, bushes or a picnic table. Heavy gear inside the corners helps too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm finding sticks now. My partner is not impressed.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Tell them you're doing a bushcraft skills session on purpose.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Probably not. But the tent will stay up, and that's what counts tonight.
